atrial_fibrillation.question: What is atrial fibrillation?
atrial_fibrillation.expected_answer: clinical overview of atrial fibrillation, focusing on diagnosis, treatment, and practice improvement

atrial_fibrillation.question: How is atrial fibrillation managed?
atrial_fibrillation.expected_answer: stroke prevention through systemic anticoagulation will be a cornerstone of atrial fibrillation management

atrial_fibrillation.question: What causes atrial fibrillation in young patients?
atrial_fibrillation.expected_answer: AF in the young is unique, with a distinct set of pathophysiologic factors that influence disease onset, response to treatment, and prognosis
atrial_fibrillation.source_title: Atrial Fibrillation in the Young: Pathogenesis and Clinical Implications.

atrial_fibrillation.question: What is the neurogenic theory of atrial fibrillation?
atrial_fibrillation.expected_answer: autonomic imbalance is not a simple modulation factor; both the trigger and the substrate of atrial fibrillation can be influenced by abnormal cardiac innervation

atrial_fibrillation.question: Is catheter ablation effective for AF in heart failure?
atrial_fibrillation.expected_answer: catheter ablation in patients with atrial fibrillation and concomitant heart failure is effective
atrial_fibrillation.source_title: Atrial fibrillation ablation in heart failure.

type_2_diabetes_mellitus.question: What is type 2 diabetes mellitus associated with?
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.expected_answer: strongly associated with lower performance on multiple domains of cognitive function and with structural abnormalities of the brain
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.source_title: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Cognitive Impairment.

type_2_diabetes_mellitus.question: What pharmacological approaches prevent type 2 diabetes?
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.expected_answer: certain drugs prevent or slow development of hyperglycemia; drugs used for obesity management were shown to prevent T2DM
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.source_title: Pharmacological approaches to the prevention of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

type_2_diabetes_mellitus.question: What is the role of gut microbiota in type 2 diabetes?
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.expected_answer: gut microbiota plays an important role in the development of metabolic diseases, especially T2DM
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.source_title: Gut Microbiota: An Important Player in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

type_2_diabetes_mellitus.question: What are the pathophysiological mechanisms of type 2 diabetes?
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.expected_answer: mitochondrial dysfunction, obesity, gut microbiota, oxidative stress and inflammation
type_2_diabetes_mellitus.source_title: Associated factors and principal pathophysiological mechanisms of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

acute_otitis_media.question: What percentage of children get acute otitis media?
acute_otitis_media.expected_answer: affects over 80% of children before their third birthday

acute_otitis_media.question: What is the first-line antibiotic for acute otitis media?
acute_otitis_media.expected_answer: Amoxicillin is the drug of choice

acute_otitis_media.question: When can antibiotic therapy be deferred in AOM?
acute_otitis_media.expected_answer: in children two years or older with mild symptoms

acute_otitis_media.question: What are the common bacterial causes of AOM?
acute_otitis_media.expected_answer: Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis

acute_otitis_media.question: What is the difference between AOM and OME?
acute_otitis_media.expected_answer: the fluid is not infected in OME as is seen in AOM patients

celiac_disease_diagnosis.question: What is the gold standard for celiac disease diagnosis?
celiac_disease_diagnosis.expected_answer: duodenal biopsy is the gold standard
celiac_disease_diagnosis.source_title: Contemporary celiac disease diagnosis: is a biopsy avoidable?

celiac_disease_diagnosis.question: What serological test is used for celiac disease?
celiac_disease_diagnosis.expected_answer: IgA anti-transglutaminase (TG2) antibodies combined with IgA quantification to rule out IgA deficiency
celiac_disease_diagnosis.source_title: Celiac disease: Understandings in diagnostic, nutritional, and medicinal aspects.

celiac_disease_diagnosis.question: What is the no-biopsy approach for celiac disease?
celiac_disease_diagnosis.expected_answer: conditional no-biopsy approach for selected adults with high-titre IgA anti-TG2 serology (≥10×ULN)
celiac_disease_diagnosis.source_title: European Society for the Study of Coeliac Disease 2025 Updated Guidelines...

celiac_disease_diagnosis.question: How many duodenal biopsies are recommended?
celiac_disease_diagnosis.expected_answer: at least four samples from the second part of the duodenum, with bulb biopsies conditionally included
celiac_disease_diagnosis.source_title: European Society for the Study of Coeliac Disease 2025 Updated Guidelines...

celiac_disease_diagnosis.question: What is the treatment for celiac disease?
celiac_disease_diagnosis.source_title: European Society for the Study of Coeliac Disease (ESsCD) guideline for coeliac disease and other gluten-related disorders.
